facts.statement: Huaxiagnathus is an extinct coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China.
facts.quote: Huaxiagnathus is an extinct genus of coelurosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous of China.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was collected from the Yixian Formation at Dabangou Village near Beipiao City in western Liaoning Province, dating to 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype (CAGS-IG-02-301, Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences, Beijing) specimen was collected from the Yixian Formation (Barremian stage, 125 million years ago) at Dabangou Village, Sihetun area, near Beipiao City, in western Liaoning Province.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Huaxiagnathus is about 1.8 meters in length.
facts.quote: The known Huaxiagnathus specimens are larger than the related Sinosauropteryx, with the largest specimen about 1.8 m in length.

facts.statement: Huaxiagnathus is distinguished from other compsognathids by a long premaxillary process overlapping the antorbital fossa, a hand as long as the combined humerus and radius, large first and second claws 167% the length of the third claw, a first metacarpal narrower than the second, and a reduced olecranon process.
facts.quote: Hwang et al. diagnosed this genus as follows: differing from all other known compsognathids in having a very long posterior process of the premaxilla that overlaps the antorbital fossa, a manus equal to the combined lengths of the humerus and radius, large manual unguals I and II which are subequal in length and 167% the length of manual ungual III, a first metacarpal which has a smaller proximal transverse width than the second metacarpal, and the presence of a reduced olecranon process on the ulna.

facts.statement: In 2004, Hwang et al. classified Huaxiagnathus as the most basal known compsognathid based on its unspecialized forearm.
facts.quote: In their 2004 description of Huaxiagnathus, Hwang et al. recovered it as the basalmost known compsognathid, as indicated by its unspecialized forearm.

facts.statement: A 2024 study by Andrea Cau questioned whether Huaxiagnathus belongs within Compsognathidae, noting it was known only from immature specimens.
facts.quote: In 2024, Andrea Cau published a study on the phylogenetics of compsognathids and immature theropods in general that called the assessment of Huaxiagnathus—known only from immature specimens—within Compsognathidae into question.

facts.statement: Cau and Paterna (2025) proposed that Sinotyrannus is a mature form of Huaxiagnathus, suggesting the latter name has priority.
facts.quote: Using an updated version of this matrix, Cau and Paterna (2025) determined that Sinotyrannus, a large coeval tyrannosauroid known from a specimen of an adult individual, was a mature form of Huaxiagnathus.

facts.statement: Huaxiagnathus is classified within the family Compsognathidae.
Huaxiagnathus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago in the Aptian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace 120 millones de años, en el Aptiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Huaxiagnathus was a small predator about 1.8 meters long, making it one of the largest compsognathids, longer than Compsognathus and the largest Sinosauropteryx specimens.
facts.quote: Huaxiagnathus fue un pequeño depredador de 1,8 metro de largo, de igual manera es de los compsognátidos más grandes, más largo que Compsognathus y los especímenes más grandes de Sinosauropteryx.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis places Huaxiagnathus at the base of Compsognathidae due to its unspecialized arms.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladistico ubica a Huaxiagnathus en la parte inferior de Compsognathidae, debido a sus brazos poco especializados.

facts.statement: The time range for Huaxiagnathus is from the Barremian to the Aptian, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus contains only one species, Huaxiagnathus orientalis, known from two immature individuals found in the Yixian Formation.
rejected.quote: The genus contains a single species, Huaxiagnathus orientalis, known from two immature individuals from the Yixian Formation.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'species Huaxiagnathus orientalis known from two immature individuals'

rejected.statement: Partially digested bones of an unidentified vertebrate were found inside the holotype specimen.
